finalText:
This is a small Node HTTP service, five files, no framework. Here's how a request flows through it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[server.js] -->|checks token| B[auth.js]
  A -->|passes user in| C[routes.js]
  C -->|reads| D[cache.js]
  D -->|on miss| E[store.js]
  C -->|writes| E
```

- **`server.js`** — starts the HTTP server, checks the login token on every request, then hands off to the routes.
- **`auth.js`** — makes and checks bearer tokens. A token is just a user id plus a signed hash, using a shared secret from the environment.
- **`routes.js`** — the small table of endpoints: get a user, list orders, add an order. Reads go through the cache, writes go straight to storage.
- **`cache.js`** — a small "remember the last 256 things" cache sitting in front of storage, to avoid repeat reads.
- **`store.js`** — the actual data, kept in memory. Each record quietly expires 15 minutes after it was last written.

One thing worth knowing: `routes.js` says writes should clear the cache, but `POST /orders` never does that. So after someone adds an order, a `GET /orders` can still hand back the old list until it ages out of the cache. Worth fixing if order lists need to stay accurate right after a write.
